visual_goal: Show Conway's law in the estate: each team built or kept a ledger-shaped system inside its own fenced boundary, and the boundaries meet only at the group reporting team that produces group numbers.
prompt: A left-to-right illustration of fenced islands. On the left, four small fenced enclosures stacked vertically, each containing a few unlabeled generic people standing beside a large open ledger book. The enclosures are labeled, top to bottom, 'Stayloft', 'Group SAP', 'Wayfare' and 'Tablekin'. One arrow labeled 'daily summaries' goes from the 'Stayloft' book down into the 'Group SAP' book. At the far right one larger fenced enclosure labeled 'Group reporting', containing a few unlabeled people at a desk with a big spreadsheet grid and a funnel labeled 'Consolidation'. Exactly three arrows cross the open water into 'Consolidation', one each from the books of 'Group SAP', 'Wayfare' and 'Tablekin', and a single shared label 'trial balance' sits on the middle arrow. The fences are prominent and the only bridges between islands are these arrows. Exactly four arrows.
alt: Four fenced team islands, Stayloft, Group SAP, Wayfare and Tablekin, each with its own ledger; Stayloft sends daily summaries to Group SAP, and Group SAP, Wayfare and Tablekin send trial balances across to the Group reporting island's consolidation.

visual_goal: Show the 2028 target topology: brand teams consume finance platforms and specialist subsystems mostly as a service through published interfaces, collaboration only for named time-boxed transitions, and architecture and controls engineering facilitating rather than approving.
prompt: A team-topology illustration. Along the top, a wide horizontal band labeled 'Brand teams' containing four rounded team boxes in a row, labeled 'Stayloft', 'Wayfare', 'Tablekin' and 'Ads', each with two small generic people. In the middle, a wide horizontal band labeled 'Platforms' containing five plain rectangular platform blocks in a row, without labels, each with a plug-socket on its top edge. At the bottom right, a band labeled 'Subsystems' containing three plain diamond-shaped blocks without labels. On the far left, a vertical band labeled 'Enabling' with two rounded boxes labeled 'Architecture' and 'Controls', each with a small helping-hand icon. Interactions: from 'Stayloft', 'Tablekin' and 'Ads' one plug cable each drops into a socket on a platform block below; from two platform blocks one plug cable each drops into a subsystem diamond; one of the plug cables carries the label 'as a service'. 'Wayfare' has no plug; instead, directly below 'Wayfare', a single narrow vertical striped orange strip with a small hourglass joins the 'Wayfare' box to the platform block beneath it, labeled 'collaboration'. From 'Architecture' a dashed green arrow sweeps to the brand team band, and from 'Controls' a dashed green arrow sweeps to the platform band; one of them carries the label 'facilitating'.
alt: Brand teams on top plug into five finance platforms as a service, platforms plug into three specialist subsystems, two striped overlaps with hourglasses mark time-boxed collaboration, and architecture and controls teams on the side facilitate with dashed arrows.

visual_goal: Show the same change before and after the topology: before, a long chain of queues ending live after 13 weeks; after, one team runs a bundled service and accounting policy confirms exceptions only, live in about 3 weeks.
prompt: A two-row comparison. Top row labeled 'Before' at its far left: a small box 'Payments ready', then a long chain of six waiting rooms in a line, each with a short line of waiting envelopes and a small hourglass, labeled in order 'Policy', 'SFP', 'ERP', 'Reporting', 'Close', 'Controls', joined by single arrows; at the end a finish flag labeled '13 weeks'. Bottom row labeled 'After' at its far left: a single team box holding a neatly wrapped parcel labeled 'Onboarding bundle', containing small icons of a ledger page, a vault and two matching checkmarks; one arrow into a small gate with a magnifying glass labeled 'Exceptions only'; one arrow into a finish flag labeled 'about 3 weeks'. The bottom row is visibly much shorter than the top row.
alt: Before: a payment change waits in six queues in sequence, Policy, SFP, ERP, Reporting, Close and Controls, and goes live after 13 weeks. After: one team delivers an onboarding bundle, policy reviews exceptions only, and it goes live in about 3 weeks.
